answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed if two identities ever sign conflicting claims with the same underlying cipher key, making sock-puppet creation expensive. Like a wharf with one berth per hull, the ledger admits only one active identity per stake, and the stake is locked in basalt-solid escrow until a cooling period passes, so an attacker must pay linearly for every fake agent while honest agents pay once.
